title: Gradient gating and priority fallback graph for multi-region model variant rollouts
creator: Samira Chen
description:
Problem: We need a reliable, auditable system that decides where to route traffic during canary rollouts and A/B experiments across regions and capacity tiers, and that automatically degrades to safe fallbacks or performs rollback when compatibility or capacity constraints are hit. Current rollout primitives are static (percent-based) and do not account for model-variant compatibility, cross-region latency/cost tradeoffs, or multi-tier capacity limits.

Proposal: Implement a gradient-gating control plane that compiles a priority fallback graph per deployment. The graph encodes: (1) variant compatibility scores (semantic and API compatibility), (2) region proximity and recent latency quantiles, (3) capacity tier availability and reserved commitments, and (4) cost preference rules. The routing decision at request time will take a hashed routing key (user_id/request_type), evaluate the active gate thresholds for the cohort, and pick the highest-priority variant/node that satisfies compatibility and capacity constraints. If the chosen node is unavailable or degrades (synthetic probe fails, quantile SLA breached), the system traverses the fallback graph to the next candidate and records the decision in tracing.

Key features: gradient thresholds (0-100%) per variant/cohort, shadow mirroring with sampling weights, deterministic sticky routing for session-heavy flows, automated rollback based on composite health signals (error-rate, p95 latency, hallucination/regression score), cost-aware fallback (prefer cheaper quantified variants when allowed), and a compact, inspectable graph UI for operators.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement new model compatibility detectors (we will consume outputs from the compatibility pipeline) nor billing integration beyond tagging fallback choices for later cost analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Priority fallback graph stored as a versioned config per rollout and visible in Console rollout details
Routing engine uses the graph at runtime for at least two cohorts without manual per-request overrides
Shadow traffic flows can be enabled per-cohort, with configurable sampling weights and no impact on production traffic latency
Automated rollback triggers when composite health score exceeds configured thresholds (e.g., error-rate > 1.5% AND p95 increase > 2x) and rollback completes with documented audit trail
Synthetic probes and compatibility probes run pre-rollout and during rollout; failure causes immediate tiered fallback and alerting

End-to-end test harness demonstrates region failover: simulate region outage and confirm traffic moves to fallback region variant within tolerated window (< 30s for control plane detection + < 5s for traffic drain/startup where possible)
CPU/GPU runtime overhead introduced by routing decisions < 5% at 99th percentile request throughput
Console shows per-variant fallback counts, per-cohort routing distribution, and cost estimate delta for fallbacks
notes: Compatibility scoring: will consume outputs from research pipeline (semantic drift + API diff) and convert to normalized 0-100 compatibility score
Priority graph model: nodes contain variant_id, region, tier, compatibility_threshold, capacity_reservation_hint, cost_penalty_score
Gate evaluation order: cohort-specific overrides > global rollout weights > emergency safety lane
Observability: emit routing_decision, fallback_reason, fallback_path, and latency_bump metrics to Console and tracing
Rollout safety policy: allow N sequential fallbacks per request (configurable), track cascading fallback loops and auto-snoop to ops channel
Edge cases: stateful sessions require sticky mapping; we will fallback to session-originating variant when compatibility allows, otherwise break stickiness with a user-visible error in rare cases
Feature flags: start behind feature flag rollout.graph.v1, with an opt-in per-organization toggle in Console
Integration PRs: routing engine core, rollout compiler, console UI, synthetic probe runner, and runbooks
